chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar narrated from his brother, peace be upon him, who said:

I asked him about a man who is naked and the time for salat (prayer) has arrived, then he finds a garment, half of which has blood on it or all of it. Should he perform salat (prayer) in it, or should he perform salat (prayer) naked? He said: "If he finds water, he should wash it; and if he does not find water, he should perform salat (prayer) in it and not perform salat (prayer) naked."

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the obligatory salat (prayer) whose time has entered
key_terms.ثَوْبًا: a garment or piece of clothing found for wearing in prayer
key_terms.دَمٌ: blood present on the garment as a form of impurity
key_terms.صَلَّى فِيهِ: he performed salat (prayer) while wearing that garment
key_terms.عُرْيَانًا: in a naked state, without clothing
key_terms.عُرْيَانٍ: naked, without clothing covering the body for prayer
key_terms.غَسَلَهُ: he washed it, meaning he cleansed the garment with water
key_terms.مَاءً: water used to wash and purify the garment

ai.seo_question: Should a person pray in a blood-stained garment if the only alternative is praying naked?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding salat (prayer) when a person has no proper clean clothing available except a garment stained with blood. It states that if water is available, the garment should be washed; otherwise, one should pray in the blood-stained garment rather than pray naked.
